AI in measurement: A one-day workshop

Source: vignettes/articles/ai-workshop.Rmd
ai-workshop.Rmd

The workshop takes a room of people who know item response theory (IRT) through the AI topics of the AI Hub in one day: Automated scoring, item text and difficulty, automatic item generation, and the audit of an AI-scored test, ending with governance and a plan for each participant’s own program. It suits 8 to 30 psychometricians, testing-program staff or graduate students who have used R. No one needs to have trained a model or used a language model before.

Everything runs offline. The four labs use simulated data with problems planted on purpose, and the language-model examples answer from recordings (mv_llm_replay()), so no API key or internet connection is needed on the day and every participant sees the same results.

Get the kit 

library(mirtverse)
kit <- copy_workshop("ai-workshop")   # slides, facilitator's guide, README
rmarkdown::render(file.path(kit, "slides.Rmd"))
rmarkdown::render(file.path(kit, "facilitator-guide.Rmd"))
File What it is
slides.Rmd The day’s slides, one section per session, with the code for each topic. Edit them to add your own program’s examples.
facilitator-guide.Rmd Preparation, the schedule, the goal of each session, what to watch for in each lab, discussion questions, and what to do when something goes wrong.
README.md What is in the folder.

The day

Time Session Material
9:00 to 9:45 AI in measurement: What changes and what does not Slides; book chapter Machine learning through an IRT lens
9:45 to 11:00 Automated scoring Lab 7, run_lab("auto-scoring")
11:15 to 12:30 Item text and difficulty Lab 8, run_lab("item-text")
13:30 to 14:45 Automatic item generation Lab 9, run_lab("aig")
15:00 to 16:15 Auditing an AI-scored test Lab 10, run_lab("ai-audit")
16:15 to 17:00 Governance, and what to do on Monday Slides; book chapter Validity, fairness and governance of AI

With half a day, keep the opening, Labs 7 and 10, and the governance session. For a semester instead of a day, the course map spreads the same material over four weeks with a book chapter as each week’s reading.

Before the day

Ask participants to install the packages and open one lab:

install.packages(c("mirt", "learnr", "remotes"))
remotes::install_github("okanbulut/mirtverse")
library(mirtverse)
run_lab("auto-scoring")

Run each of the four labs to the end yourself, with the answer key in Teaching labs open, and read the facilitator’s guide. Labs work best in pairs.

Make it yours

  • Your own data. The instructor toolkit builds labs with AI sections on your own items or your own engine’s scores, which can replace a built-in lab in the afternoon.
  • Your own examples. The slides are plain R Markdown: Add a slide on an AI use in your program, or a live model with mv_ask_setup() if your room has internet and your data can leave it.
  • An assistant. The teaching assistant can adapt the slides or build a lab for you from a plain-language request.
